subject: AtlasOps / Redwood — reference architecture fit assessment

From: Nadia Petrova <nadia@atlasops.io>

Subject: AtlasOps x Redwood: quick check on reference architecture fit

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for taking a call last week. We sketched a compact reference blueprint that wires AtlasOps' inference gateway in front of a multi-variant Redwood deployment (hosted + dedicated fallback) and wanted to confirm there are no unexpected compatibility gaps before we spin up a proof-of-concept.

High-level:
- Low-latency routing to Redwood hosted API (primary)
- Fallback to a dedicated pool via mutual TLS for high-throughput flows
- Shared observability via a small shim that emits token-level telemetry to a dedicated topic

I attached the initial blueprint (atlasops-reference-blueprint-v1.pdf) and a short matrix of the API calls we expect to exercise. Can Marissa or someone on the solutions team confirm whether the approach looks feasible from a serving/runtime perspective, and flag any testing we should do early?

We can be flexible on test harnesses — we have a harness that can replay production-like prompts and measure tail latency if you want it.

Best,
Nadia Petrova
Head of Integrations, AtlasOps
partners@atlasops.io

Nadia —

Appreciate the blueprint. Quick read looks promising. Looping in Marissa (solutions) and Sergio (partner engineering) to validate runtime/observability assumptions and enumerate the minimal test cases we'd need for a gate review.

High-level questions off the bat:
- Does the AtlasOps gateway terminate TLS and re-encrypt to Redwood, or does it pass through client certs?
- Are you planning to use KV cache hints from the gateway, or will caching be managed only by Redwood?
- Can your harness emit CSVs with per-token timings and a trigger ID we can correlate to our traces?

If Marissa/Sergio are good, let's propose a 2-week POC scope and a short MAP (mutual action plan).

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Subject: Re: AtlasOps x Redwood: quick check on reference architecture fit

Nadia —

Thanks for the blueprint and the context. I pulled this into an internal checklist and added a few notes; attaching our working checklist (redwood-interop-checklist.xlsx) with candidate test vectors. Summary of technical observations:

1) TLS / auth model
- Prefer pass-through of client identity to Redwood when possible (mTLS with token exchange). If AtlasOps terminates and reissues client credentials we need to add token mapping and trace propagation to maintain per-tenant observability and quota scoping.

2) Caching expectations
- If AtlasOps wants to manage prefix caching at the gateway we need agreed semantics for KV hint headers. Otherwise, keep caching at Redwood and add a small cache-control header AtlasOps can set.

3) Streaming and chunking
- Redwood's runtime prefers continuous batching for streams. If AtlasOps breaks streaming into many small connections it can hurt batching efficiency; recommend pooling at the gateway side.

4) Metrics and correlation
- We can accept a CSV export with token timings and a correlation id. Ideally the harness also POSTs a lightweight JSON trace to our ingestion endpoint to correlate request-level traces.

Suggested minimal POC scope (2 weeks):
- Week 1: Connectivity + auth model validation (mTLS + token mapping), basic latency sweep
- Week 2: Streaming throughput test + failover to dedicated pool + telemetry correlation test

Please confirm whether the AtlasOps team can run the CSV export and whether you can share a small set of test prompts. I attached the checklist for you to mark.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: AtlasOps x Redwood: quick check on reference architecture fit

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and exactly the level of detail we wanted. Quick answers below and next steps: 

- TLS/auth: AtlasOps can operate in pass-through mode with mTLS to Redwood; we'll exercise token mapping in Week 1 of the POC.
- Caching: We'll keep caching at Redwood for the POC and send cache-hint headers in 10% of requests to validate behavior.
- Streaming: We'll configure connection pooling to avoid fragmenting streams; our harness will emulate pooled clients.
- Metrics: We can emit CSV per test run and POST a small trace JSON to the ingestion endpoint.

Attaching an updated blueprint (atlasops-reference-blueprint-v2.pdf) with minor flow tweaks and a link to our test harness repo.

Test prompts: we'll send a sanitized set of 50 prompts (low/med/high complexity) by EOD. Can you confirm an S3 location or endpoint we should push CSVs to?

Best,
Nadia

- Week 2: Streaming throughput + dedicated pool failover test; CSV export + trace correlation
- Deliverables: success matrix (pass/fail per checklist row), POC readout slide deck, optional next-step pricing sketch

I've attached a short MAP doc to capture owners and dates (MAP-AtlasOps-Redwood-20270719.docx). Sergio: can you own the failover run? Marissa: please own the trace ingestion setup. Nadia: please upload the prompt set and schedule a daily 9:30am PST sync for the next two weeks.
